title: Factor Polynomials: Trinomials and Difference of Squares
description: Factor as reverse multiplication: remove the greatest common factor, then use sum-product pairs and difference-of-squares patterns to factor completely.

questions.stem_html: Which choice gives the complete factorization of \(x^{2}+10x+21\) over the integers?
questions.explanation_html: Remove the common factor 1 if needed. The constants 3 and 7 add to 10 and multiply to 21, so the result is \((x+3)(x+7)\).
questions.variation: Choose a sum-product pair with positive factors

distractor_notes.B: Changes the sign of the middle term.
distractor_notes.C: Uses a pair with the wrong sum and product.
distractor_notes.D: Changes one factor and no longer reproduces the polynomial.

questions.variation: Choose matching negative signs or opposite signs

distractor_notes.A: Changes the sign of the middle term.
distractor_notes.B: Uses a pair with the wrong sum and product.
distractor_notes.C: Changes one factor and no longer reproduces the polynomial.

questions.stem_html: Which choice gives the complete factorization of \(x^2-81\) over the integers?
questions.explanation_html: After the GCF 1, the inner expression is a difference of two squares with square roots \(x\) and \(9\). The opposite signs cancel the two middle products, giving \((x-9)(x+9)\).

distractor_notes.A: Introduces a middle term that is not in the original.
distractor_notes.B: Uses equal signs and introduces a middle term.
distractor_notes.D: Changes one factor and no longer expands back.
